policy.patch: 0.x.y contains compatible fixes and narrowly necessary tests/documentation. A bug label or migration alone does not settle compatibility.
policy.priority_legend: P1: consequential security/integrity or required production evidence; P2: moderate affected-workflow risk; P3: later improvement. Priority is assessed here, not a GitHub label or a release-necessity score.
policy.size_legend: S: bounded surface; M: several paths or a race; L: cross-layer/client/deployment work. These are planning estimates, not day commitments.

standing_rules: Every PR that changes a 0.5.1 issue updates release-data.json, appends a row to execution.md and re-runs render.py in the same PR.
Every PR keeps docstring coverage at or above 80% for the functions in each file it creates or edits, counted before the first push.
Run refresh.py before render.py whenever GitHub milestones or issue states have changed. refresh.py reads GitHub only and never writes to it.

decisions.question: Does #909, battery and equipment authorization residuals, stay in 0.5.1?
decisions.answer: No. Moved to vNext: the issue is unscheduled and waits on the battery and equipment rework.

decisions.question: Which backlog items join 0.5.1?
decisions.answer: A new restore-drill issue for gate R5 (#1010) and #252, unreachable code. #133 stays unassigned.

decisions.question: Where does the 0.5.1 dashboard live?
decisions.answer: A new dated directory, release-planning/2026-10-19. The 0.5.0 plan in release-planning/2026-10-15 stays frozen.

decisions.question: How does the Vale baseline prune land, now that master accepts only pull requests (#988)?
decisions.answer: The workflow opens or updates a pull request from chore/vale-baseline-prune using GITHUB_TOKEN. The maintainer enables "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" and closes and reopens each prune pull request to start its checks.

decisions.question: May the calendar 500 body carry the user-supplied event title (#989)?
decisions.answer: No. The body is the fixed message; the title, type and id go to the server log.

decisions.question: Does the userfile name-existence signal on upload need a fix (#991)?
decisions.answer: No. Accepted as a residual in ADR-0048 item 9. The first rationale offered said DELETE revealed the same signal; it does not (204 either way). The maintainer kept the acceptance on the corrected reasoning.

decisions.question: How do the four open 0.5.1 issues proceed?
decisions.answer: #900 is waiting on ADR-0049 acceptance, not on new design work. #904 lands the existing -x5-b migration as one PR rather than a caller-by-caller subset. #252 starts with a record correction, because WebhookRunner was deleted while accepted ADR-0024 says it stays. #1010 runs in its own session. Drafts are in issue-responses-2026-10-20.md.

decisions.question: Is ADR-0049 accepted?
decisions.answer: Yes, part 1, on the maintainer's motion. Part 2 decides nothing and stays open, so #900 stays open until the comment correction lands. Acceptance is PR #1019, which carries only the lifecycle edits; its dashboard row lives here.

decisions.question: How is ADR-0024's WebhookRunner claim corrected (#252)?
decisions.answer: By a superseding record, ADR-0051, as the maintainer directed. The InfluxDB writer never called WebhookRunner (Guzzle directly since 296d99dd), so ADR-0019's original last-caller statement stands. ADR-0051 also proposes removing the webhook residue: three unused catalogue strings, one docstring and plan 20's curl row.
